native.previewCaveat: HTML previews are illustrative light-mode shape and color translations, not native Liquid Glass simulations or pixel-exact iOS rendering. Browser focus and hover rules support the preview only. SwiftUI, native glass optics and SF typography remain authoritative. Comparison boards are conceptual multi-device images.
native.rampCaveat: Tonal ramps are synthesized OKLCH panel previews, not implemented application color scales.
native.units: Geometry uses native points; semantic type sizes resolve at runtime.
native.accessibilitySessionEditor: At accessibility text sizes, date/time labels stack above controls, clear actions have independent rows with 44pt minimum height, and timezone labels and values stack.
native.primaryButton: PrimitiveButtonStyle wrapping .glassProminent; .capsule; .large; semibold subheadline; explicit PrimaryButtonText foreground. Native sizing and states.
native.secondaryButton: PrimitiveButtonStyle wrapping .glass; .capsule; .large; semibold subheadline; explicit AccentColor foreground.
native.sidebarMaterial: Regular glass with AccentColor at 0.08 opacity, 26pt rounded rectangle and 10pt outer inset; opaque SurfaceBackground when Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast is active.
native.navigationMaterial: Automatic system navigation and tab bar backgrounds.
native.completionActions: Job detail uses native bottom safeAreaBar with 20pt horizontal and 10pt vertical padding; primary completion action and circular glass More menu.
native.scopeControls: Upcoming uses native menu picker; Jobs status retains native segmented picker.
native.sidebarSymbols: Unselected sidebar symbols explicitly use appearance-aware AccentColor; selected symbols use Color.white. Native selection tint remains forest SidebarSelection.

narrative.overview:
Cuekeeper pairs a date-led working agenda with quiet paper surfaces, forest accents and a warm charcoal night palette. The approved Combined Glass direction uses Quiet Glass as its base, an expressive floating iPad sidebar and rounded native glass actions. Its hierarchy supports quick capture, incomplete schedules and independent booking, coverage and payment states. The stacked cue-card mark and native SF typography retain the identity.

This records the implemented SwiftUI system, grounded in `Cuekeeper/DaybookStyle.swift`, the color assets and the existing screen implementations. The approved boards in `design/branded/` supply the composition and hierarchy direction; `design/liquid-glass/implementation-brief.md` records the combined material direction. The multi-device comparison boards are conceptual images. Native system glass optics, SF typography, navigation, tabs, sheets, pickers and menus remain authoritative; this is not a claim of pixel equality with the boards.
keyCharacteristics: Date-led agenda rows with clear booking badges.
Titled detail pages and compact ruled panels.
Forest and mint accents on ivory and warm charcoal.
Native glass actions and a floating iPad navigation surface.
Native controls and Dynamic Type throughout.

rules.name: The Appearance Pair Rule
rules.body: Use the named color assets so light and dark roles change together.

rules.name: The Native Type Rule
rules.body: Preserve semantic text styles and scalable supporting geometry instead of freezing the reference board's text size.

rules.name: The Quiet Reading Rule
rules.body: Keep agenda rows, forms, status badges and financial panels matte; reserve expressive glass for navigation and actions.

dos: **Do** preserve the date-led hierarchy and sessions-before-billing detail order.
**Do** use named appearance-aware color assets and semantic text styles.
**Do** keep USD and EUR separate and show real partial balances and pending schedules.
**Do** retain native controls, navigation and accessibility adaptation.
**Do** keep reading surfaces matte and let native glass define action and navigation depth.
donts: **Don't** flatten the implementation into a palette-only treatment of generic forms.
**Don't** substitute sample board data for financial or calendar truth.
**Don't** force three columns at accessibility text sizes.
**Don't** treat conceptual system chrome as a pixel-exact native requirement.
